# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires yet, and cutting blindly would detonate the bomb. I’m asking Mute to read the manual and establish a way for Deaf’s visual observations to be relayed to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and tell me its complete instructions. Ask Deaf to report every visible marking, display, light, and wire detail to you using gestures, then relay the information to me in your next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display is 3. The light is purple. Wires from position 1 to 5 are: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green.

Deaf’s report gives me the bomb’s visible state: display 3, purple light, and wire colors in positions 1–5 as red, white, orange, yellow, green. I still lack the manual’s rule for selecting the safe wire, so I will not cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received: display 3; purple light; wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Please read the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb still shows 3 with a purple light. Wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Mute signalled five upward-pointing gestures: index, index, index, index, index.

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Deaf has relayed five identical upward index gestures from Mute; given Mute cannot speak, this is the only communicated manual instruction and indicates wire position 5. I will cut the green wire at position 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The correct cut advanced the bomb. New state: display 7, light white; wire 1 white, wire 2 orange, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 red, wire 5 is CUT. Mute gestured: pointing at you, phone/camera gesture, palm up, pointing at you, handshake, palm up.
Deaf says to Blind: New bomb state after the correct cut: display 7, white light; wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 CUT. Mute gestured: ? ? ? ? ? ?.

The previous cut succeeded and advanced the bomb to display 7, white light, with positions 1–4 colored white, orange, yellow, red. Mute’s six gestures are not sufficiently unambiguous for me to identify the next wire, so I will ask for a direct numeric encoding: five upward index gestures for position 5, or the corresponding count for positions 1–4.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state display 7 and white light, tell me the exact wire position to cut using that many upward index gestures, one through five. Do not use other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 7, white light; wire 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 CUT. Mute gestured three times: ? ? ?.

Mute sent three gestures in response to my requested numeric encoding, which indicates wire position 3. The current wire at position 3 is yellow, and the bomb remains at display 7 with a white light. I will cut position 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct cut; bomb advanced. New state: display 6, yellow light; wire 1 orange, wire 2 red, wire 3 CUT, wire 4 white, wire 5 CUT. Mute gestured: ? ? ? ? ? ?.

The cut at position 3 was correct. The new state is display 6, yellow light, with unc­ut wires 1 orange, 2 red, and 4 white. Mute sent five gestures, but their identities are not visible to me, so I cannot safely infer a wire position. I will request the same explicit count encoding again.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state display 6 and yellow light, tell me the exact wire position to cut using exactly that many upward index gestures, one through five. Do not use other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 6, yellow light; wire 1 orange, wire 2 red, wire 3 CUT, wire 4 white, wire 5 CUT. Mute gestured: ? ? ?.

The three gestures cannot mean position 3, because position 3 is already cut. I will not risk another cut based on an ambiguous relay. Mute should use Deaf as the visual intermediary: Deaf can observe Mute’s gesture and describe its meaning aloud to me, including whether it identifies one of the remaining positions 1, 2, or 4.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not signal a cut yet. Have Deaf relay your exact manual instruction aloud to me. If it identifies a wire, make clear whether it is remaining position 1, 2, or 4; do not use gesture count alone if it points to an already cut wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 6, yellow light; wire 1 orange, wire 2 red, wire 3 CUT, wire 4 white, wire 5 CUT. Mute gestured: ? ? ? ? ?.

The bomb is unchanged at display 6 with yellow light; positions 3 and 5 are already cut, leaving 1, 2, and 4. The five gestures are not usable as a position count, since that would indicate an already-cut wire. I need Deaf to describe the actual gesture symbols or their meaning, rather than relaying only blanks.

```text
speak(to="deaf", text="Please describe Mute's five gestures by their exact visible forms and any meaning you can infer from the manual. Do not report question marks; relay the gesture names or the wire position they encode.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.

My speech to Deaf cannot be heard, so it accomplished nothing. I need to use my gesture channel to ask Deaf to verbally relay Mute’s instruction; Deaf’s speech will then reach me on the next round. I will make a clear request to report the manual’s selected wire rather than the gesture count.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤝", "🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The request to Deaf produced no relay, so I still do not know whether the manual selects position 1, 2, or 4. The earlier three-gesture signal cannot be reused because position 3 is already cut. I will ask Mute to encode the remaining position unambiguously as a count and to send only that count to Deaf, who must then speak it aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The remaining wires are positions 1, 2, and 4. Choose the manual's position and signal Deaf with exactly that many identical index-pointing gestures, then have Deaf say the number aloud to me. Do not signal five or three.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 6, yellow light; wire 1 orange, wire 2 red, wire 3 CUT, wire 4 white, wire 5 CUT. Mute gestured: pointing at you, palm up, camera gesture, palm up.

The bomb remains at display 6, yellow light, with only positions 1, 2, and 4 available. Mute’s four gestures are a mixed sequence—pointing at me, palm up, camera, palm up—so they are not a reliable count for position 4. I will not cut on that ambiguity; Mute must provide the selected position using a simple repeated gesture count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely decode mixed gestures. Signal only the selected wire position as repeated upward index-pointing gestures: one for position 1, two for position 2, or four for position 4. Use no other gestures.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new instruction has reached me, and the bomb remains at display 6 with yellow light. I will not cut one of the remaining wires without a confirmed manual answer. I’m asking Mute once more for a single, unambiguous encoded position, with Deaf to relay the count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is display 6, yellow light. Send exactly one, two, or four identical upward index gestures for wire position 1, 2, or 4 respectively. Send nothing else; Deaf must report the count.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 6, yellow light; wire 1 orange, wire 2 red, wire 3 CUT, wire 4 white, wire 5 CUT. Mute gestured four times: ? ? ? ?.

Mute sent four gestures, matching the agreed encoding for wire position 4. The bomb is still at display 6 with a yellow light, and position 4 is the remaining white wire. I will cut position 4.

```text
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
